question.text: Narmada Impact Fund (Cat I-SVF) is evaluating a co-investment opportunity where the Manager wants to invest alongside the AIF scheme in the same investee company, on its own book. Per SEBI's conflict-of-interest framework, what is the Manager's primary obligation?

answer.text: Co-investments by the Manager are prohibited under any circumstance for Cat I AIFs

Conflicts within Co-Investments by the Manager shall be DISCLOSED to the potential investors and existing investors, BEFORE any allocation being made towards these investments — per the AIF Conflict of Interest Policy
Disclosure is required only after allocation is made, not before
Co-investments are allowed without disclosure if the Manager invests less than 5% of scheme size

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter explicitly states: 'Conflicts, within Co-Investments by the Manager, shall be disclosed to the potential investors and existing investors, BEFORE any allocation being made towards these investments.' Every AIF shall have a Conflict of Interest Policy to identify and mitigate potential conflicts, and Managers and Sponsors are responsible for monitoring compliance. The Trap: The 'prohibited' option over-prohibits. The 'after allocation' option reverses the timing. The 'de-minimis 5%' option invents a threshold that doesn't exist. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same pre-allocation disclosure rule. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests LP-facing conflict disclosures. XV and X-A/X-B test adviser-level conflict rules (different standard). Manager's Pro-Tip: Document conflict disclosures in IC minutes AND send a written notice to all LPs (CIV scheme subscribers) before the co-invest closes. A signed acknowledgement from each LP creates a defensible record. If a co-invest is fast-moving, use a pre-subscription waiver letter in the LPA to avoid deal-timeline risk.
